newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: CLT-UFA, Kirch to share Premiere.
newsitem.headline: CLT-UFA, Kirch to share Premiere.

text.p: CLT-UFA and rival Kirch Group said in a joint statement they had agreed to be 50-50 partners in German digital pay-television broadcaster Premiere.
France's Canal-Plus, which now holds 37.5 percent of Premiere, is satisfied with the deal, the statement said.

The deal resolves a long-running struggle for position in the budding German digital television market. Kirch holds 25 percent of Premiere, while Bertelsmann's CLT-UFA and Canal-Plus each hold 37.5 percent.

"CLT-UFA and the Kirch Group agreed over the weekend to end the squabbles in the German pay-TV market and to pursue the development of pay-TV, particularly the digital market, together," the joint statement said.
"Only by combining our forces can the German digital market be developed on an internationally comparable scale in an economically sensible way."
Under the deal, Kirch would supply Premiere's film content and set-top decoder box, and develop Premiere as a digital broadcaster parallel to Kirch's DF1 digital station.

The partners continue to hold talks with Deutsche Telekom AG about tying the decoder technology into Telekom's cable network. They foresee an offering of over 50 digital channels and expect to reach the needed agreements in the next several weeks, they said.
